rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-047 (illustrative figures), A-1: at the old landed price import demand (about 650,000 t) exceeds the 400,000 t of licences, so the marginal tonne pays the 60% rate and the quota binds; foreign supply is from many exporters (A-4, p = 0.85), so the sellers abroad do not absorb the rate.
No matching assumption in WE-047; judged from the text: domestic beet sugar supplies about 1,100,000 t of the 1,750,000 t consumed and is the same good as imported white sugar, which sets its price.
